# gyro_firewall (Resource)

Network firewall of a server (requires the Network Firewall add-on). Works like an AWS network ACL / ufw: rules are evaluated in the given order and the first match wins; default_action applies to inbound traffic that matches no rule. The resource owns every customer rule of the server: apply replaces them, destroy removes them (default allow). Rules applied by Gyro support are not managed here. Gyro Cloud servers (engine = cloud): allow rules only, default_action deny, inbound only, no destination or country sources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Web server: 80/443 open to everyone, SSH only from the office, everything else denied.
resource "gyro_firewall" "web" {
  server_id      = 1234
  default_action = "deny"

  rule {
    action      = "allow"
    protocol    = "tcp"
    port        = "80,443"
    description = "web"
  }
  rule {
    action   = "allow"
    protocol = "udp"
    port     = "443"
  }
  rule {
    action = "allow"
    port   = "22"
    source = "203.0.113.10"
  }
}

# Database: open, but 3306 closed to one address; outbound SMTP blocked.
resource "gyro_firewall" "db" {
  server_id      = 1235
  default_action = "allow"

  rule {
    action = "deny"
    port   = "3306"
    source = "198.51.100.7"
  }
  rule {
    direction = "out"
    action    = "deny"
    port      = "25"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `server_id` (Number) Server id.

### Optional

- `accept_warnings` (Boolean) Apply even when the API reports warnings (lock-out risk, shadowed or duplicate rules, private sources). Without it such a change fails and lists the warnings.
- `default_action` (String) Default rule (*) for inbound traffic that matches no rule: allow or deny.
- `permanent` (Boolean) Make each change permanent at once (default). false = the change is a 5 minute trial that reverts unless confirmed in the panel or via the API.
- `ping` (Boolean) Answer ping (ICMP echo).
- `rule` (Block List) Rules in evaluation order (first match wins). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))

### Read-Only

- `engine` (String) network (Istanbul core router) or cloud (provider firewall).
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `status` (String) none, applying, trial, active, open, removing.

<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Optional:

- `action` (String) allow or deny.
- `description` (String) Up to 60 characters.
- `destination` (String) any (all IP addresses of the server) or one IP address of the server.
- `direction` (String) in (to the server) or out (new outbound connections; source = remote address).
- `port` (String) any, 22, 80,443 or 1000-2000 (not for icmp/all).
- `protocol` (String) tcp, udp, tcp_udp, icmp or all.
- `source` (String) any, an IPv4 address/CIDR or a comma separated list, country:TR or not-country:TR (country add-on).
- `type` (String) rule, brute_force (port = protected ports) or port_scan.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import gyro_firewall.web 1234
```
